definitions.explanation: A defensive ditch filled with water surrounding a castle or fortification.

examples.japanese: {城|しろ}の{周|まわ}りには{深|ふか}い{堀|ほり}がある。
examples.english: There is a deep moat around the castle.

examples.japanese: {江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}の{堀|ほり}が{今|いま}も{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: Moats from the Edo period still remain today.

examples.japanese: {外|そと}{堀|ぼり}と{内|うち}{堀|ぼり}で{守|まも}られていた。
examples.english: It was protected by an outer and inner moat.
examples.notes: Note rendaku: ほり → ぼり in compounds

notes:
KANJI VARIATIONS:
・{堀|ほり} - moat, canal (man-made waterway)
・{濠|ほり} - moat (often used for castle moats)

HISTORICAL CONTEXT: Moats were essential defensive structures for Japanese castles ({城|しろ}). Many castles had multiple moats ({外|そと}{堀|ぼり} outer moat, {内|うち}{堀|ぼり} inner moat).

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
・{外|そと}{堀|ぼり} (outer moat)
・{内|うち}{堀|ぼり} (inner moat)
・お{堀|ほり} (moat - polite, often refers to Imperial Palace moat)
・{堀|ほり}{端|ばた} (moatside)

PLACE NAMES: Many Tokyo place names include {堀|ほり}:
・{日本橋|にほんばし}{堀留|ほりどめ}
・{虎ノ門|とらのもん}{外堀|そとぼり}
